answer: Because the vertex liability is published in the beacon ledger at admission, the ripple audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind each duplicate self it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. A sponsor carries 38% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. That is 17 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
